answer: Three tasters judge each wine blind, and every one of them stakes his reputation on the verdict. A lotus bottle swapped in from another estate fails the panel: the tasters know the estate's own wine by taste, and a foreign bottle is named at the signal of the first sip. Staging a false tasting costs a forger 13,100 in bribes to tasters who would lose their standing, and the dune mark on the tasting sheet follows the bottle, so a wine that fails the panel cannot be entered again under a new name.
